6 The partnership firm initially consisted four partners namely Sh. Diwan Chand Jain, Gian Chand Jain, Sardari Lal Jain & Pyarelal Jain, all sons of Late Sh. Jagan Nath Jain.

The said land was also mutated in the revenue record in the name of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand and all the legal heirs of the erstwhile partners of the partnership concern namely M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand are entitled to a specific share in the amount of compensation as per the order passed by Sh. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed vide order dated 20.09.2022:-
1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to th entire amount of compensation of the acquired property sent in the present reference petition?
OPP 2.
Whether the respondent is entitled to receive the entire amount of the acquired property sent in the present reference petition?
OPD 3.
Whether the awarded amount is to be apportioned between the parties?
Onus on parties 4.
Relief.

11 During the pendency of the present reference petition, one partner of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain, namely Suraj Prakash Jain expired and an application for the impleadment of legal heirs was filed.

A perusal of the record shows that though said application was moved on 10.05.2019, but his LRs could not be impleaded, however I have seen the NOC/affidavits filed by the LRs namely Smt. Sushma Jain and Smt. Sonia Jain in favour of LR Sh. Shashi Kumar Jain and allow the present application holding that Sh. Shashi Kumar Jain shall be entitled to receive the awarded amount of compensation in terms of judgment passed by Sh. AK Sarpal, Ld. ADJ dated 17.07.2015.
12

During the pendeney of the present reference petition, one of the persons / partner of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain filed a separate claim petition stating that he is the owner of 1/3 rd share undivided share [20.5%] in an area admeasuring 7000 sq. yds. in village Jhilmil Tahirpur Delhi.

He further claimed that one Smt. Lajwanti Jain died on 28.02.1975 leaving behind her will dated 19.8.1973 and codicil dated 23.05.1975 wherein her share was purportedly inherited by the male heirs of deceased Rajender Kumar Jain.

He further claimed that a share title of 6.834% be given to him in terms of the directions passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in WP[C] No.8136/15 vide order dated 16.01.2018 and further claimed that Sh. Kailash Kumar Jain, Subhash Kumar Jain &
Satish Kumar Jain should specifically agreed that Smt. Lajwanti trust has come to an end and then be allowed to take 1/3rd share as per Codicil dated 23.05.1974.
He further claimed that he be allowed to take partition of the released land and he be allowed to deposit the requisite stamp duty as per law.
13 Ld. counsel for I.P. No.1 has filed written arguments in support of her contentions.
However, IP No.2 namely M/s Tirupati Enterprises has neither filed written argument, nor addressed oral arguments despite giving several opportunities.
Union of India is just a proforma party in the present case.
14 I have perused the written arguments as filed by ld. counsel for I.P. No.1.
15 I have also perused the record.

sentences.text: All these issues are being taken up together being inter- connected.
The matter was posted for evidence of the parties.
M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain through Sh. Shashi Kumar Jain filed its evidence by way of affidavit Ex.IP1W1/A in which the witness IPW1 deposed on the same line as that of their claim petition.
The witness on behalf of the recorded owner namely M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain filed the copy of the registered sale deed which is Mark A (colly.).
The said witness also filed the copy of dissolution deed as well as the copy of the judgment passed in WP[C] No.8136/2015 dated 16.01.2018 which is Mark-B (colly.).

The said witness also filed the copy of order dated 17.07.2015 passed by Sh. A.K. Sarpal, Ld. ADJ with respect to the apportionment of compensation among all the legal heirs of the erstwhile partners of IP No.1 namely M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain which incorporated the percentage of each partner which he/she was liable to receive.
The said judgment was marked as Mark-D.

The witness further deposed that the IP No.2 namely M/s Tirpurati Enterprises was never in possession of the acquired property and the said property was never sold to M/s Tirupati Enterprises at any point of time.

The witness further deposed that the sale deed filed by M/s Tirupati Enterprises is clear with respect to the fact that no acquired portion of the land in khasra No.1184/20, Jhilmil Tahirpur Delhi was ever sold to it.

17 The said witness exhibited his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.IP1W1/A and appeared several times for his cross examination, however he was not cross examined by M/s Tirupati Enterprises and the entire evidence of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain was proved being unrebutted.
18 The IP No.2 namely M/s Tirupati Enterprises was also given ample opportunity to lead evidence and to prove its claim, however M/s Tirupati Enterprises failed to prove its claim.

The sale deed filed by M/s Tirupati Enterprises along with its claim has never been proved in order to establish its claim over the compensation sent in the present reference petition and is therefore, rejected.
19 I have also perused the claim petition filed by one of the legal heirs of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain namely Sh. Neeraj Kumar Jain S/o Late Sh. Darshan Lal Jain.

At the very outset, the claimant Sh. Neeraj Kumar Jain has himself admitted that he is the owner of 1/3 rd undivided share out of 20.5% in land bearing Khasra No.1184/20 and this percentage is equivalent to 6.83% and the same corroborates the percentage already awarded by Sh. A.K. Sarpal, Ld. ADJ in case titled UOI Vs.
Jagan Nath Diwan Chand bearing M. No.61/14.
20

After perusal of the order dated 17.07.2015, it is evident that the claimant herein namely Sh.
Anand Kumar Jain, Amar Jain & Neeraj Kumar Jain appeared in person and gave statement with respect to the apportionment of the compensation pertaining to M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain which also pertained to the same Khasra number i.e. 1184/20, Jhilmil Tahirpura Delhi.

After recording the statement of all the parties, a table reflecting the percentage of each parties was formulated in order dated 17.07.2015 which is being reproduced herein under:-

The said percentage was agreed by all the parties /
partners / legal heirs of erstwhile partners of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain and as per the said agreed percentage, the amount of compensation sent in the said reference petition was eventually distributed and received by all the parties.

The claimant Sh. Neeraj Kumar Jain, though admitting his share to be 1/3rd out of 20.5% [i.e. 6.83%] has further claimed that the other partners of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand namely Sh. Kailash Chand Jain, Sh. Subhash Chand Jain & Satish Kumar Jain are not liable for receiving the agreed percentage since there was allegedly a Will dated 19.08.1973 and a Codicil dated 23.05.1975 of late Smt. Lajwanti Jain.

None of the documents mentioned in the claim have been proved in the said proceedings and the claimant namely Sh.
Neeraj Kumar Jain
has himself admitted the percentage payable to him.

The judgment passed by Sh.
AK Sarpal, Ld. ADJ dated 17.07.2015 has been duly acted upon and all the beneficiaries of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain had already received the awarded amount of compensation in accordance with the said order.

Neither Sh. Neeraj Jain nor any other beneficiary of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain has ever impugned the order dated 17.07.2015 and it appears that Sh. Neeraj Jain had only tried to mislead this Court by filing such claim petition. 22

Since M/s Tirupati Enterprises has failed to prove its claim in this court over the acquired property and also not rebutted any of the evidence filed by M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain, I hereby hold that the entire amount of compensation sent in the present reference petition pertaining to land bearing Khasra No.1184/20/2/1, Jhilmil Tahirpur, Delhi along with any amount of structures mentioned in the award be paid to the beneficiaries of M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain as per the shares already agreed and acted upon vide order dated 17.07.2015 passed by the court of Sh. Ashwini Kumar Sarpal, Ld. ADJ in M. No.61/2014. 23

Needless to say that the IP no.1 namely M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand Jain would also be entitled to all the statutory benefits as per the provisions of Land Acquisition Act along with proportionate interest U/s 34 of the L.A. Act, 1984.
Issue no.1 to 3 are decided in favour of the IP no.1 namely M/s Jagan Nath Diwan Chand.
24 Reference is answered accordingly.
Parties to bear their own costs.
Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
File be consigned to Record Room as per rules.

RAMESH  RAMESH KUMAR  KUMAR
